books.title: The Red Tent
books.author: Anita Diamant
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: Tells the story of Dinah, Jacob's only daughter, from her own point of view, growing up among the four wives of Jacob. Readers praise its rich picture of daily life, childbirth and women's customs in the ancient Near East. It departs freely from Genesis in places and has mature content, which you chose to keep it with in mind.
books.bible: Genesis 34 gives Dinah only a few verses. The novel imagines her side of the events at Shechem and the family life of Leah, Rachel, Bilhah and Zilpah.

books.title: Counted With the Stars
books.author: Connilyn Cossette
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: An Egyptian girl sold into slavery to a Hebrew-hating household witnesses the plagues from the Egyptian side and must decide whether to leave with Israel. Readers like how it makes the plagues feel real and frightening, and how it handles faith with warmth.
books.bible: Exodus 12:38 says 'a mixed multitude' left Egypt with Israel. The heroine is one of them.

books.title: A Lineage of Grace
books.author: Francine Rivers
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: Five short novellas about the women named in Jesus' genealogy in Matthew 1: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, Bathsheba and Mary. Readers find it moving and close to Scripture, with study questions at the end of each story. Its stories span several eras.
books.bible: Matthew 1 surprisingly names these women among Jesus' ancestors. Each novella follows one woman's Old Testament story.

books.title: Shelter of the Most High
books.author: Connilyn Cossette
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: A young woman flees raiders and finds safety in Kedesh, one of Israel's cities of refuge, soon after the conquest. Readers enjoy learning how the cities of refuge worked, alongside the romance and adventure.
books.bible: Numbers 35 and Joshua 20 set up six cities of refuge, where someone who had killed by accident could live safely until a trial.

books.title: Michal
books.author: Jill Eileen Smith
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: The story of Saul's daughter, who loved David, saved his life, was married to another man and was later taken back. Readers find it sad but sympathetic, and a good look at court life under Saul and David.
books.bible: Michal is one of the few women the Bible says loved a man (1 Samuel 18:20). Her story ends in sorrow in 2 Samuel 6.

books.title: The Secret Chord
books.author: Geraldine Brooks
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: David's life told by the prophet Nathan, from shepherd boy to old king. It is a literary novel praised for its language and its unflinching picture of a violent age. It has graphic and mature content and takes liberties with the text, which you chose to keep it with in mind.
books.bible: Nathan appears at key moments in David's story: the covenant in 2 Samuel 7, the rebuke over Bathsheba in 2 Samuel 12, and Solomon's anointing in 1 Kings 1.

books.title: The Legend of Sheba
books.author: Tosca Lee
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: Imagines the queen of Sheba's life and her famous journey to test Solomon's wisdom. Readers enjoy its lush writing and strong heroine. It adds a romance the Bible doesn't mention and has some mature content, which you chose to keep it with in mind.
books.bible: 1 Kings 10 and 2 Chronicles 9 describe the queen's visit, her hard questions and her praise of Israel's God. Jesus mentions her in Matthew 12:42.

books.title: Gods and Kings
books.author: Lynn Austin
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: Young Hezekiah grows up under his idol-worshipping father Ahaz and becomes the king who leads Judah back to God. It is the first book of the Chronicles of the Kings series. Readers say it brings the books of Kings to life and makes the history easy to follow.
books.bible: 2 Kings 16 describes Ahaz's idolatry. 2 Kings 18 and 2 Chronicles 29–31 tell of Hezekiah's reforms.

books.title: Return to Me
books.author: Lynn Austin
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: A family follows the first group of exiles home from Babylon to rebuild Jerusalem and the temple. It is the first book of the Restoration Chronicles. Readers value how it shows the hardship and hope of the return.
books.bible: Ezra 1–6 records Cyrus's decree and the rebuilding of the temple. The prophets Haggai and Zechariah urged the builders on.

books.title: Hadassah (One Night With the King)
books.author: Tommy Tenney
books.list: Old Testament list
books.review: Esther's story told as a sweeping court drama in the Persian palace at Susa. Readers enjoy the suspense and the details of royal life, and it was made into a film.
books.bible: The book of Esther explains the origin of the festival of Purim and shows God's care for his people, though it never names God.

books.title: The Source
books.author: James Michener
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: An archaeological dig at a fictional mound in Galilee uncovers layers of history, and each layer opens a story from the Stone Age to modern Israel. It is long and full of history. Readers call it a great way to see the whole sweep of the land's past.
books.bible: Several episodes are set in biblical times, including the age of the patriarchs, David's kingdom and the Maccabees.

books.title: Sarah
books.author: Orson Scott Card
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: Follows Sarah from her youth through her marriage to Abraham, the years of waiting and the birth of Isaac. Readers find it thoughtful and true to the spirit of Genesis while filling in her inner life.
books.bible: Genesis 12–23 follows Abraham and Sarah from Haran to Canaan and Egypt, and to the promise fulfilled in Isaac.

books.title: The Pharaoh's Daughter
books.author: Mesu Andrews
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: The Egyptian princess who drew baby Moses from the Nile grows up in the royal court and comes to know Israel's God. Readers praise its research into Egyptian life and its gentle faith.
books.bible: Exodus 2 tells of Moses' rescue. 1 Chronicles 4:18 mentions a 'daughter of Pharaoh' named Bithiah who married into the tribe of Judah.

books.title: Isaiah's Daughter
books.author: Mesu Andrews
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: A war orphan raised in the prophet Isaiah's household becomes the wife of King Hezekiah. Readers love how it brings Isaiah's prophecies and the Assyrian crisis into a personal story.
books.bible: 2 Kings 21:1 names Hezekiah's wife Hephzibah. The novel imagines her life during the Assyrian siege of 701 BC.

books.title: Harvest of Rubies
books.author: Tessa Afshar
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: A gifted scribe in the Persian court, a cousin of Nehemiah, is given in marriage to a nobleman and learns about love and faith. Readers enjoy the court setting and the humour.
books.bible: Nehemiah 1–2 opens in the Persian palace at Susa, where Nehemiah served as the king's cupbearer before going to rebuild Jerusalem's walls.

books.title: Ben-Hur
books.author: Lew Wallace
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: A Jewish prince betrayed by his Roman friend survives the galleys, wins the famous chariot race and finally meets Jesus. Written in 1880, it was one of the best-selling American novels of its century. Readers still find its ending powerful.
books.bible: It opens with the magi's journey (Matthew 2), and Jesus appears at key moments, including the crucifixion.

books.title: The Bronze Bow
books.author: Elizabeth George Speare
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: An angry young Galilean wants to drive out the Romans until he meets a carpenter teacher in Capernaum. It is a Newbery Medal winner written for young readers, and adults enjoy it too.
books.bible: It draws on Jesus' early ministry around Capernaum, including the healings and the calling of the fishermen in Mark 1–6.

books.title: Pontius Pilate
books.author: Paul L. Maier
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: A historian's novel of Pilate's career as governor of Judea, built closely on the ancient sources. Readers praise how much real history it teaches.
books.bible: Pilate's trial of Jesus is told in all four Gospels, most fully in John 18–19.

books.title: The Secret of the Kingdom
books.author: Mika Waltari
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: A wealthy Roman arrives in Jerusalem at the crucifixion and sets out to learn whether the reports of the resurrection are true. Readers like its searching, thoughtful tone.
books.bible: It follows the days after Easter, from the empty tomb to Jesus' appearances in Galilee (John 21).

books.title: The Robe
books.author: Lloyd C. Douglas
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: The Roman tribune who won Jesus' robe at the cross is haunted by it and sets out to learn about the man who wore it. It was a best-seller in the 1940s and became a famous film.
books.bible: John 19:23–24 tells how the soldiers cast lots for Jesus' seamless robe.

books.title: Quo Vadis
books.author: Henryk Sienkiewicz
books.list: More in the vein of Ben-Hur
books.review: A Roman officer falls in love with a Christian woman during Nero's reign, as Rome burns and the persecution begins. Peter and Paul both appear. Its author won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1905.
books.bible: It takes up where Acts 28 ends, with Paul in Rome. The title comes from a tradition that Peter met Jesus on the Appian Way and asked, 'Quo vadis?' ('Where are you going?').
